chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the prayer in Mecca.
He said: Whoever wishes, he completes (the prayer), and whoever wishes, he shortens (it).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening or completing prayer in Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the permissibility of both completing (tamam) and shortening (qasr) prayers within the sacred precincts of Mecca, reflecting the scholarly consensus that the restriction of shortening applies only to traveling outside the city limits. It highlights the flexibility granted to worshippers in the Haram, distinguishing Mecca's unique status from other travel destinations in Shia jurisprudence.
